messages:
Jordan (Sales): Heads-up — FinServe on today's call asked for a hybrid billing product: committed tokens + prepaid 'cushion' credits to cover spikes. They want a predictable blended per-token rate for procurement. Need product + billing input this week.

Elaine (PM): Got it. Can you paste their usage profile and constraints here? I need commit size, expected spike multiplier, gen vs embedding mix, SLOs, region, contract length, and whether the cushion should auto-burn before overages or act as a throttle. I want to add acceptance criteria before we put this in the backlog.

Jordan (Sales): Copying notes from call:

```
Customer: FinServe
Commit: 300,000,000 tokens / month
Expected peak multiplier: up to 2.5x for seasonal month
Mix: ~60% generation, 40% embeddings
Latency SLO: 300ms p50 for generation
Region: eu-west (data residency required)
Contract: 12 months
Preferred billing: prepaid cushion credits that are consumed on spike; clear blended effective rate; avoid surprise invoices
Procurement deadline: Thu EOD
```

Mike (Support): FYI I created an internal support ticket with the transcript. Customer is firm about avoiding surprise overage bills and asked for invoice examples. Also flagged EU residency + compliance questions.

Nora (Product Ops): Clarifying Qs: 1) When you say "prepaid cushion that is consumed on spike", do they expect the cushion to be deducted before overage charges are applied (i.e., invoice shows zero overage until cushion is exhausted)? 2) Do they want cushion to auto-refill or be one-time? 3) Should usage reporting surface cushion burn separately in the console? We need precise billing behavior to write acceptance criteria and UI copy.

Alex (Eng): Technical implications: burst behavior and achievable latency differ between Hosted and Dedicated. If they need 300ms p50 during 2.5x spikes, we may have to route traffic to Dedicated pools or provide an explicit burst SLA (and charge for it). That impacts implementation complexity and cost. For a pilot we can scope only the billing math + invoice/UI changes and defer routing/SLA infra.

Elaine (PM): Draft acceptance criteria to add to PRIC backlog (feel free to edit):
- Define terms: "commit" (prepaid token bucket per month), "cushion credits" (prepaid buffer applied before overage), and "overage" (what triggers extra billing).
- Billing math: worked example with numbers showing commit usage, cushion burn, and overage calc; show rounding rules and token unit granularity.
- Invoices/UI: sample invoice line items and console display for cushion balance and burn events.
- Behavioral mapping: Hosted vs Dedicated behavior when cushion is exhausted (fallback: overage billing vs throttling vs route to Dedicated); document recommended default for pilot.
- Contract language: sample SLA/terms for pilot and renewal pricing impact.

Jordan (Sales): Customer wants a written proposal this week for procurement. Can product give rough effort estimate and a pilot plan?

Alex (Eng): Rough estimates: billing math + invoice UI annotations = ~1 sprint (engineering + qa). Dedicated routing + SLA + infra changes = additional 2-3 sprints. For quick response, we can offer pilot that implements prepaid cushion bookkeeping and invoicing only; surface routing/SLA as an optional add-on (follow-up work).

Nora (Product Ops): I'll open the intake ticket and tag billing/legal. Fields I added: customer, commit tokens, peak multiplier, token mix, SLO, region, contract length, preferred billing behavior, procurement deadline.

Jordan (Sales): Filled intake: FinServe | 300M | 2.5x | 60/40 gen/emb | 300ms p50 | eu-west | 12mo | prepaid cushion. Attaching PO draft to the ticket now.

billing-bot: Created PRIC-7890: https://issues.redwood.co/PRIC-7890 — assigned to @Elaine (PM), labels: pilot, pricing-intake, legal-review

Elaine (PM): Thanks. I'll draft a minimal pilot scope and acceptance criteria in PRIC-7890 and propose sample pricing bands (blended per-token effective rates) by EOD Friday. Jordan — please attach the procurement deadline and PO. Nora — add billing/legal reviewers. :thumbsup:
